title: Live socket reply
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.2, #773), not implemented. Capture's answer to one request (capture-socket-request.schema.json), on the same connection, as a frame with `t` `reply` and the request's `id`. `ok` true: capture has applied it (the app then records it in the wish, which is what makes it outlive a restart of capture). `ok` false: nothing was changed; `error` says why and `confirm` whether the refusal only needs the person's yes (then `error` is the question, and the client asks again with `args.confirm` true under a new id). A repeated id gets this same reply again. No reply ever carries a secret.

ok.description: true: applied (or answered, for an op that changes nothing). false: refused, nothing changed.

error.description: With `ok` false: why. Text for a person (`refused: parked`, `refused: taken`, a question when `confirm` is true), or one of the words a client acts on: `stale` (a squelch apply whose `expect` is not what runs), `expired` (it arrived after `expires_boot`), `unsupported` (an op capture does not know), `forbidden` (a viewer's request; `credentials` from a peer that is not uid 0).

confirm.description: With `ok` false: true when the refusal only needs the person's yes.

result.description: With `ok` true, for an op that returns something: `urgent_since` (`$defs/urgent-since-result`), `snapshot` (capture-socket-event.schema.json `$defs/snapshot`), `probe` (`audio` or `none`). The reply does not name its op: the client knows it by `id`.

urgent-since-result.title: The result of urgent_since
urgent-since-result.description: One page of the urgent rows above the asked cursor.

urgent_epoch.description: The urgent file's epoch now, 16 hex characters. Not the one asked for: the file was reset and the rows are from 0.

rows.description: The rows above the cursor in `n` order, at most `limit`; each with `durable` true.

more.description: There are more rows: ask again from the last `n`.

memory.description: On the first page: the items capture holds that have no row (yet), in full, each with `n` null and `durable` false. They move no cursor.
